thread:
anya: FYI asia2 started showing degraded GPU pool and ~30% 502s after the region BGP announcement at 09:12 UTC. I'm switching traffic but want to call out DNS TTL behavior.

mike: seeing the same. We did a staged failover (weight 80->20) but some customers still hit old ip. Possibly resolver caches with long TTLs.

jia: which records did we update? A record for inference.redwood.ai pointing to asia2-lb -> failover-lb? Any NS changes?

ethan: we only updated the A for inference.redwood.ai to the failover ELB IP at 09:13:04 UTC. No NS change. TTLs were 300s on the org zone, but some internal resolvers seem to be honoring a longer effective TTL (cache jitter).

ops-oncall: rolling incident note: gpu-pool degraded, autoscaler not reacquiring nodes due to quota in us-west, doing cross-region burst to asia1/eur1. See ops runbook step 3 for DNS strategy.

anya: quick tests: dig +short inference.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8 -> returns old ip from asia2 for some queries. dig +trace shows glue servers returning new ip. Looks like intermediate resolvers cached the old A beyond 300s.

mike: suspecting DNS propagation race. When we did the weight shift we also lowered TTL to 60 but that only helps new queries, not entries already cached.

natalie: customers on corp resolvers reported 502 spikes until ~09:28. That lines up with cached entries expiring. Problem: if we lower TTL in emergency mid-failover, it doesn't flush caches.

jia: workaround idea: create a short-lived CNAME inference.redwood.ai -> failover-shunt.redwood-internal and set the CNAME TTL low, then point failover-shunt to the failover LB. But depends on client resolver behavior for CNAME caching.

ethan: another option: add a second A record for inference.redwood.ai with ipv4 of failover and keep the old one for a few minutes (dual-homing) so clients that still resolve old ip still get traffic via our edge NAT if possible. But risk: asymmetric routing + stickiness issues.

ops-oncall: for this incident we did a staged plan: 1) lower TTL to 60 (done 09:14) 2) issue weighted traffic shift 09:15 -> 09:20 3) add failover A record as duplicate 09:16 4) monitor 502 rate and rollback if error > 5%.

mike: monitoring shows 502 rate dropped to baseline after 09:30, but there was a 10m tail. We should document TTL-jitter guidance in runbook: do not rely on mid-change TTL reduction to solve propagation.

anya: capturing a quick repro of resolver behavior:

```
# from corp-resolver (internal)
$ dig @10.1.5.3 inference.redwood.ai A +short
203.0.113.12  # old asia2

# from public
$ dig +short inference.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
198.51.100.22  # new failover
```

mike: also saw some clients use stale EDNS0 cache that returned old edns-client-subnet -> routing to asia2 and failing. EDNS0 makes caching more fragmented.

natalie: notes for postmortem: - TTLs: keep emergency low-ttl baseline for critical records (30-60s). - For planned failovers, do pre-lowered TTLs 24h in advance where possible. - Document CNAME vs duplicate A tradeoffs.

ethan: follow-up action: runbook update PR in docs repo and add a checklist to Dedicated failover runbook. Also add a monitoring alert for resolver-MX cache mismatch.

deploy-bot: deploy status: runbook/ttl-guidance.md created by @ethan, awaiting review.

ops-oncall: closing the active mitigations. Assigning postmortem to @mike. If anyone has logs showing clients stuck > 10m, drop them here.

mike: will do a correlate between ingress logs and resolver logs, ping if I need access. :thumbsup:

anya: thanks team — incident declared mitigated at 09:34 UTC, but we'll capture action items and timeline in the postmortem.
